name: Hot 'n Now
notice: A layout study, not Hot 'n Now: its website rebuilt with Golden Grids as GIFn'now, a parody name, in the chain's legacy colours. Not affiliated with Hot 'n Now; nothing can be ordered and no form sends anything.
summary: The five pages of hot-n-now.com (home, menu, about, careers and locations) rebuilt as stacked golden grids, with the content of the brand as it is today and the look of the brand as it was in the 1990s.

reviewed.method: Read and captured at 390, 820 and 1440 pixels. The legacy look is taken from three files on Wikimedia Commons: the 1992 logo, and two photographs from 2014 of a former restaurant and of the drive-thru board in Sturgis, Michigan.

real: The menu, the two addresses, the telephone number, the stated values, the owners and the facts in the answered questions, as the restaurant's site gave them.
The history before the relaunch, from Wikipedia's article on the chain.
invented: Every sentence, which is the study's own. None of the site's copy or slogans is used.
The look. It is a reading of the old brand from one logo and two photographs, not the chain's current or official design, and the bolt is the study's own drawing.
The order builder and the bag. The site lists no prices, so none are shown, and nothing is ordered or sent.
The food photographs, which are not of the restaurant's food. Only the olive burger is the named dish, from another Michigan kitchen.
The brand. GIFn'now is a parody name made for this study; it is not the restaurant.
The closing form. The site's asks for contact details as well as an email; this one keeps a single email box and sends nothing.
